questionsApplications.label: How should climate change, migration, AI and international development be governed, and what do economics, political institutions and ethics each contribute to that policy analysis?

What professional and career directions -- policymaking, political leadership, think-tank and policy consulting, journalism and academic research -- does a combined philosophy-politics-economics training prepare graduates for?

alternatives.concept: Ethical agency, emotion and philosophical argument are studied alongside economic models of markets, public policy and decision-making. Five dedicated Philosophy courses and six Economics courses provide sustained substance, supported by political foundations and quantitative and qualitative research. Sociology, rights and communication provide companion perspectives; they do not reproduce VU integrated PPE-in-Practice modules or its compulsory thesis.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The organising question changes disciplinary weight, not just a label. Against ucr-1: 9 exclusive courses (67.5EC) each way. Three qualified responses are supported by sustained disciplinary substance, not general coherence. Primary has five dedicated Philosophy courses37.5EC plus political philosophy7.5 and six Economics courses45EC; theories of ethics, agency and emotion interact with micro/macro, public, behavioural and empirical economic analysis. Second has five Politics courses37.5EC and six Economics45EC, plus WesternPhilosophy/Ethics15EC; international relations, EU institutions, conflict, law and historical context alter the organising priority to institutions and political economy. Third has five Philosophy37.5 and five Politics37.5, rights/constitutional/international law and qualitative/social enquiry; economic foundations remain7.5EC, a stated limitation. This third official pairing can recombine existing courses: rejection merely because no unused catalogue remains was invalid. Each pair differs by at least four courses/30EC; the changed disciplinary weights follow distinct questions, not arbitrary padding. None reproduces VU recurring integrated Practice, specialist philosophy-of-science/history sequence, complete methods trajectory, supervised Tutorial or compulsory individual thesis. These gaps remain substantial and explicit, but UCR actual sustained philosophical, political and economic study materially addresses the target rather than replacing its defining objects with adjacent fields.

alternatives.concept: Philosophical agency, ethical reasoning and rights are examined alongside comparative politics, international relations, EU institutions and conflict. Five Philosophy and five Politics courses supply the main weight, complemented by law and qualitative enquiry. Introductory Economics preserves a limited economic foundation; this is a Philosophy-and-Politics response, with less economics depth and no VU supervised thesis or integrated Practice sequence.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 names three specialisations (Philosophy, Politics, Economics) and Article 11.4 requires every student to follow exactly two of them; the normalized target is the generic bachelor and names no specific pair. All three pairings share an identical60ECofYear1common units plus12ECof sharedYear2Practice and an identical Year-3 structure, and combine exactly two disciplines to the same depth (two compulsory courses per chosen specialisation plus four restricted electives, at least one per chosen track), so no pairing is more representative of the programme's broad academic identity, and none is less specialised, than another under the curriculum page, future page or OER Article 10.1's own symmetric description of the three disciplines. The OER's Appendix 1 (Programme overview) prints exactly three annual-plan tables in a fixed order -- 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & ECONOMICS', then 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & POLITICAL SCIENCE', then 'TRACKS POLITICAL SCIENCE & ECONOMICS' -- so the official-order tie-break selects the first-listed pairing, Philosophy & Economics, fixed before any UCR course was considered and independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three qualified responses are supported by sustained disciplinary substance, not general coherence. Primary has five dedicated Philosophy courses37.5EC plus political philosophy7.5 and six Economics courses45EC; theories of ethics, agency and emotion interact with micro/macro, public, behavioural and empirical economic analysis. Second has five Politics courses37.5EC and six Economics45EC, plus WesternPhilosophy/Ethics15EC; international relations, EU institutions, conflict, law and historical context alter the organising priority to institutions and political economy. Third has five Philosophy37.5 and five Politics37.5, rights/constitutional/international law and qualitative/social enquiry; economic foundations remain7.5EC, a stated limitation. This third official pairing can recombine existing courses: rejection merely because no unused catalogue remains was invalid. Each pair differs by at least four courses/30EC; the changed disciplinary weights follow distinct questions, not arbitrary padding. None reproduces VU recurring integrated Practice, specialist philosophy-of-science/history sequence, complete methods trajectory, supervised Tutorial or compulsory individual thesis. These gaps remain substantial and explicit, but UCR actual sustained philosophical, political and economic study materially addresses the target rather than replacing its defining objects with adjacent fields. Generator rows5102–5111,5122,5123,5125 are owned by closest or the coherent political-economy candidate. Third is independently justified by official structure, not a new residual interest category. Career/problem examples5126–5136 remain search-only; no climate/AI/career promise generates an extra programme.

notes.text: These alternatives develop sustained philosophy, politics and economics in different proportions. They do not reproduce VU integrated PPE-in-Practice sequence, specialist philosophy of science and advanced political philosophy, complete methods sequence, supervised Tutorial or compulsory individual thesis. The Philosophy-and-Politics option has only introductory economics. Optional UCR independent research adds study outside the scheduled 180 EC; it is not a promised substitute for the VU thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Philosophy, Politics and Economics examines social questions through philosophical argument, political analysis and economics. Students study all three disciplines, specialise in two, practise research methods and interdisciplinary application, and complete an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three qualified UCR alternatives emphasise philosophy and economics, political economy and governance, or philosophy and politics. Each develops sustained disciplinary study, with different companion fields. VU integrated applications, specialist units and compulsory supervised thesis remain substantial differences.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration selects Ethics II and International Trade in period 4, History of Philosophy II and Global Justice in period 5, qualitative methods and an approved 30 EC study-abroad package. Completing 120 EC in Years 1–2 and 30 EC abroad before the Tutorial and thesis satisfies both published entry thresholds. Approval, attendance, academic-English, progression and thesis-registration rules apply; future course themes and offerings can change.
